slot.brief: For a matrix of the form I + A with A² = A (or nilpotent A), derive a closed form for (I + A)^n and evaluate a specific power using the pattern.

verdicts.working: I+A=\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}. Its fifth power has diagonal entries 2^5 and 1, and upper-right entry 2(1+2+4+8+16)=62.

working:
$A^2=A\Rightarrow (I+A)^n=I+\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom nk A=I+(2^n-1)A$.
For $n=5$: $(I+A)^5=I+31A=\begin{bmatrix}32&62\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$.

Independent check: I+A=\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}. Its fifth power has diagonal entries 2^5 and 1, and upper-right entry 2(1+2+4+8+16)=62.

draft.distractor_notes: B: uses $I+nA$ instead of the binomial coefficient sum. C: uses $2^nA$ rather than $(2^n-1)A$. D: omits the factor $2$ in the off-diagonal entry of $A$.
